title: Local acyclicity identifies the closed-fibre restriction of the derived unit
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $G$ an abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Suppose $f$ is locally acyclic relative to $G$ [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf]. Fix a geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-geometric-point], put $S'=S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and use the canonical lift of $\bar s$ over the closed point of $S'$ [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1). Let $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\to S'$ be any geometric point. Set $X'=X\times_SS'$, $p:X'\to X$, $X_{\bar s}=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $X_{\bar t}=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $i:X_{\bar s}\to X'$ and $h:X_{\bar t}\to X'$. Write $G'=p^{-1}G$ and $G_{\bar t}=h^{-1}G'$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and place sheaves in degree zero in the bounded below derived categories of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $\beta:G'[0]\to Rh_*(G_{\bar t}[0])$ be the unit of the derived adjunction $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction], using derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and derived inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]. Then the canonical morphism
$$i^{-1}\beta:i^{-1}G'[0]\longrightarrow i^{-1}Rh_*(G_{\bar t}[0])$$
is an isomorphism in $D^+(\operatorname{Ab}((X_{\bar s})_{\mathrm{et}}))$. Neither properness nor torsion of $G$ is required.

proof.text: At each geometric z and in degree zero, apply the unit-germ comparison. Local acyclicity makes alpha an isomorphism; cancel the two comparison isomorphisms to obtain invertibility of the actual stalk map.

For q>0 the exact inverse image of the source single complex has zero homology. Apply the target-stalk comparison and the positive cohomology vanishing in local acyclicity to kill the target. For q<0 the source single complex has zero homology, and the nonnegative right-derived functor plus exact inverse-image/homology compatibility kill the target. A map between zero objects is invertible.

Use the ulift geometric-stalk natural isomorphism to pass to the stalks in the geometric-stalk conservativity theorem. Every cohomology-sheaf map is invertible; apply the bounded-below cohomology isomorphism criterion.
